quotes.quote: A (coverage-)guided fuzzer for dynamic language interpreters based on a custom intermediate language ("FuzzIL") which can be mutated and translated to JavaScript.
When fuzzing for core interpreter bugs, e.g. in JIT compilers, semantic correctness of generated programs becomes a concern.
semantic correctness can easily be worked around by wrapping the generated code in try-catch constructs.
The fuzzer is implemented in Swift, with some parts (e.g. coverage measurements, socket interactions, etc.) implemented in C.
MutationFuzzer: produces new programs from existing ones by applying mutations.
Corpus: stores interesting samples and supplies them to the core fuzzer.
Evaluator: evaluates whether a sample is interesting according to some metric, e.g. code coverage.
Storage: stores crashing programs to disk.
The fuzzer is event-driven, with most of the interactions between different classes happening through events.
Fuzzilli uses a custom execution mode called REPRL (read-eval-print-reset-loop).
execute it, then reset its internal state and wait for the next script.
To scale, fuzzer instances can form a tree hierarchy
one root instance, 16 intermediate nodes connected to the root, and 256 "leaves" connected to the intermediate nodes.
See the Targets/ directory for the list of supported JavaScript engines.
Compile the engine with coverage instrumentation (requires clang >= 4.0) as described in the README.
A paper from the NDSS Symposium 2023 about Fuzzilli and how it compares to other fuzzers.
